rubric.why: Identifies the kind of information stored in the head section.
Gives the title or another example of document information.
rubric.description: Says it can contain information such as the document title.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the title or another suitable example.

modelAnswer: This section contains meta-information about the HTML document, like the title.

rubric.description: States that an ordered list is numbered.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking ordered lists with numbering.

rubric.description: States that an unordered list is bulleted.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking unordered lists with bullets.

modelAnswer: You can create ordered (numbered) and unordered (bulleted) lists.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming at least one of inline or internal CSS.

rubric.why: Includes the external method, completing the three methods when combined with the first point.
rubric.description: Names external CSS as a method; the three methods are inline, internal, and external.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming external CSS.

modelAnswer: Integrating CSS with HTML is essential for styling web pages and it can be done in three primary ways: inline, internal, and external styles.

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML anchor tag used to create links.
rubric.description: States that hyperlinks are created using the <a> tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the anchor tag.

rubric.why: Recognises the href destination attribute and the link's closing or displayed text structure.
rubric.description: Gives the href attribute as part of the hyperlink syntax.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including href and a valid link structure or its destination and text.

modelAnswer: Links are created using the `<a>` tag.

rubric.why: Identifies the link tag and its location in the document.
rubric.description: Says the external CSS file is linked using <link> in the <head>.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the link tag in the head section.

rubric.why: Identifies the stylesheet relationship and the external file reference.
rubric.description: Includes the stylesheet and href attributes in the link element.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for including the stylesheet and href details.

modelAnswer: The most efficient method for larger projects is to use an external CSS file, which is linked to the HTML document with the `<link>` tag in the `<head>` section.

rubric.why: States that tables present data in an organised structure.
rubric.description: Says tables display data or information in a structured format.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying structured data display.

rubric.why: Gives the stated benefits of comparing and organizing information.
rubric.description: Mentions easy comparison and organization of information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating comparison and organization as benefits.

modelAnswer: Tables in HTML are used to display data in a structured format, allowing for easy comparison and organization of information.

rubric.why: Identifies the script element used to include JavaScript.
